title: Malmstrom missiles disabled by red glowing object
summary: Jesse Michels tells of Malmstrom missiles disabled by red glowing object, about 1967 at Malmstrom AFB, Montana, and relays what a named person told them. As told, not a fact.

tellings.quote: You have Robert Salas at Malmstrom saying that the whole base was actually rendered inoperable.
can look at in the 1960s the Readiness status change at of our icbms at malstrom Air Force Base where missiles were taken offline
tellings.difference: Gives only 'the 1960s', with no red glowing object and no credit to Robert Salas.
tellings.link_reason: Both describe ICBMs at Malmstrom AFB being taken offline in the 1960s.

as_told.title: Malmstrom ICBMs taken offline
as_told.place_text: Malmstrom Air Force Base, Montana, USA

tellings.quote: and uh just as I told him our missiles began going into what's called a no-go condition or unlaunchable essentially they were disabled
tellings.difference: Gives the date as March 24, 1967, describes the missiles going no-go as Salas reported the object, and credits Fred Meiwald.
tellings.link_reason: Both tell of the 1967 Malmstrom missiles going offline during a red glowing object sighting, as Robert Salas told it.

as_told.title: Malmstrom missiles go no-go during red object sighting

tellings.quote: on job control they have a wall and they have green lights where all the missiles are on alert except for one corner all 10 missiles were off alert all 10 whole flight was off alert all red
tellings.difference: Told by Bob Jamison, who says a whole flight of 10 missiles showed red on the job control wall.
tellings.link_reason: Jamison describes the same 1967 Malmstrom event in which missiles were taken off alert, seen on the job control board.

tellings.quote: And I've met some I met Robert Salis at Malmstrom in 1967. You know, that was his sighting uh where, you know, 10 of these sites were were disarmed according to him.
tellings.difference: Says 10 sites were disarmed according to Salas, and that Michels met him.
tellings.link_reason: Same 1967 Malmstrom missile shutdown, told by Robert Salas.

tellings.quote: Arie Arnoldson who was the the uh the actual commander of the the the Mal uh the Montana uh base
tellings.difference: Names the base commander, Arie Arnoldson, as filing a UFO report with NORAD, and ties him to John Mack.
tellings.link_reason: Same 1967 Malmstrom event in which a whole flight of 10 Minuteman missiles went off alert.

as_told.title: Malmstrom: the commander filed a UFO report with NORAD after 10 Minuteman missiles were shut down

tellings.quote: I do think it's interesting with this with this Malmstrom case, I think there's a lot of circumstantial evidence to to say that this this actually happened.
tellings.difference: Credits Robert Hastings and points to circumstantial evidence, without describing the event itself.
tellings.link_reason: This is the same 1967 Malmstrom missile-disabling case.

tellings.quote: it's almost like taking matches out of the hands of a baby, you know.
tellings.difference: Told by James Fox, crediting Tim Coleman and the film Out of the Blue, with no base named and a 'matches from a baby' framing.
tellings.link_reason: Robert Salas's account of UFOs disabling missiles at a 1960s nuclear missile base is the Malmstrom story told from Salas.

as_told.title: Robert Salas on UFOs over nuclear missile bases

tellings.quote: and I came across a 2010 Robert Hastings press conference where he had six people from the Air Force, various positions in the Air Force. The first one was Robert Solace talking about UFOs disabling nuclear missiles at Monstrom Air Force Base
tellings.difference: Told by way of Salas's testimony at Robert Hastings's 2010 press conference with six Air Force witnesses.
tellings.link_reason: Robert Salas's account of the Malmstrom missiles being disabled in 1967 is the same incident the story holds.

as_told.title: Robert Salas at the 2010 Hastings press conference: Malmstrom missiles shut down

tellings.quote: But when you have multiple witnesses like so Malmstrom, let's use the 1967 case. You have Bob Salis, he's at Oscar uh launch control center.
tellings.difference: Names Oscar Flight specifically and stresses that there were multiple witnesses.
tellings.link_reason: Both are the 1967 Malmstrom missile shutdown as Robert Salas witnessed it from the Oscar Flight launch control center.

as_told.title: Malmstrom Oscar Flight missile shutdown (Bob Salas)

tellings.quote: Bob Salace incident at Malmstrom uh nuclear base in 1967 where he was at Oscar um you know launch facility underground and uh you had this red orb over top and and nine out of 10 missiles went into no go mode under his watch
tellings.difference: Names the Oscar launch facility and says nine out of ten missiles went down, where the story's tellings say all ten.
tellings.link_reason: Both describe the 1967 Malmstrom incident in which Robert Salas's missiles went into no-go status while a red object was overhead.

as_told.title: Malmstrom 1967 missile shutdown during a red orb sighting

tellings.quote: before I could tell them about the phone calls, we get a big horn go off. One of the missiles went off alert status or went from green to red.
tellings.difference: Told firsthand by Salas with an exact date (March 24, 1967) and the alarm horn as the first missile went from green to red.
tellings.link_reason: Salas's own account of the March 1967 Oscar Flight missiles going off alert while a red glowing object was seen. The Malmstrom story already holds Salas and Meywald tellings of this event.

as_told.title: Oscar Flight missile shutdown during UFO sighting
as_told.place_text: Oscar Flight launch control center near Roy, Montana (Malmstrom AFB)

tellings.quote: like the intervention you saw at Melmstrom in ' 67
tellings.difference: Only a passing mention, with no details.
tellings.link_reason: The same 1967 UFO interference with the missiles at Malmstrom.

related.note: The Wall Street Journal explains the same 1967 Malmstrom missile shutdown as an EMP rather than a UFO, a competing core claim about the same event.
